jobs.occupation: Junior Fermentation Scientist (m/f/d) (Data Scientist)
jobs.description: Your missionWe are seeking a motivated Junior Fermentation Scientist to join our biotechnology team and support the development and optimization of microbial fermentation processes. This is a hands-on laboratory role with a strong focus on planning and executing fermentation experiments, from shake-flask cultivation to bench-scale fermentations.You will work independently at the clean bench, prepare andoperate fermentation experiments, and monitor relevant process parameters and performanceindicators. Your responsibilities will also include analyzing key process and product KPIs using bioanalytical methods such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, and HPLC, as well as evaluating, documenting, and reporting experimental results.The role offers a high degree of autonomy in organizing your day-to-day laboratory work, with responsibility for ensuring that experiments are thoroughly planned, executed, analyzed, and documented. You will contribute directly to improving our microbial fermentation workflows and advancing robust and scalable bioprocesses.• Plan, prepare, and perform microbial cultivation and fermentation experiments, ranging from shake-flask cultures to bench-scale fermentations of up to 5 L• Carry out laboratory work under aseptic conditions, including work at the clean bench and the preparation of culture media, buffers, solutions, and reagents• Set up, operate, monitor, and maintain bench-top fermentation systems and associated laboratory equipment• Monitor fermentation performance and evaluate relevant process and product KPIs throughout experimental campaigns• Perform bioanalytical characterization of fermentation samples using methods such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, HPLC, and other relevant analytical techniques• Evaluate experimental data, identify trends and deviations, and summarize results in a clear and structured manner• Document experiments thoroughly and learn how to prepare concise reports of experimental results and conclusions• Organize and prioritize your laboratory activities independently, ensuring that experiments are properly planned, executed, analyzed, and documented within agreed timelines• Contribute to the maintenance and organization of microbial strains, cell banks, laboratory materials, and equipment• Collaborate closely with colleagues across different disciplines and contribute to the continuous improvement of our fermentation processes and laboratory workflowsYour profile• A degree or vocational qualification in biotechnology, microbiology, bioprocess engineering, biological laboratory technology (e.g. BTA), or a related field• Practical experience working under aseptic conditions and confidence in standard microbiological and biotechnology laboratory techniques• Hands-on experience with microbial cultivation; experience with shake-flask cultures and/or bench-scale fermenters is highly desirable• Familiarity with the preparation of culture media, buffers, solutions, and reagents, as well as accurate sample handling and laboratory documentation• Experience with, or a strong interest in learning, analytical methods for evaluating fermentation samples, such as SDS-based analysis, enzymatic assays, and HPLC• A structured and reliable approach to experimental work, with the ability to independently organize laboratory activities and follow experiments through from preparation to data analysis and reporting• A practical, hands-on mindset combined with curiosity, attention to detail, and a willingness to troubleshoot and learn new techniques• A collaborative and team-oriented approach, while being comfortable taking ownership of assigned experiments and project tasks• Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken; German is a plusOur Benefits:• Work for one of the global innovation leaders in the food industry.• Dynamic and diverse mission-driven team from more than 25 different countries.• A fast growing company with exceptional opportunities for personal development.• Flat hierarchies and short decision paths.• Flexible working hours with entitled Home Office days in an innovative and agile working environment.• Gym Membership, language classes or an attractive alternative from our benefit program.• Great team events such as “Lunch & Learn”, “Demo Day”, cultural celebrations and food tastings.• Drinks, cereal bar and fresh fruit at the office, our home products tasting session for new employees.• Lastly, join us in the journey as we change the food system as we know it!We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. Ready to disrupt the food system with us?About usInfinite Roots® is a biotech company based in Hamburg, Germany. We tackle some of the world’s biggest challenges through products we develop by leveraging the fungal kingdom. Our team of 60+ people from 25 nationalities — 55% women and 10 PhDs strong — shares one mission: to unlock the full potential of fungi for a more sustainable future.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activity (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the field of solar physics and planetary research with around 300 employees. The interdisciplinary research focus is the investigation of the development, diversity and dynamics of planets, moons, small bodies, the sun and solar-like stars. The MPS develops and operates scientific instruments for current and future space missions (e.g. ESA, NASA), and carries out cosmochemical laboratory investigations of meteorites as well as numerical modeling on state-of-the-art supercomputers.The Department Solar & Stellar Interiors at MPS invites applications for the position of aPostdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to characterize young star-planet systems and their flaring activityIn recent years, exoplanetary science has undergone a major shift -- moving from exoplanet detection towards understanding star-planet systems as a whole, including the host star, interplanetary medium and galactic context. Specifically, tidal and magnetic interactions between planets and their host stars have been recognized to be able to modulate the evolution of both, including the atmospheric evolution of the planet and its habitability. The newly established ERC StG project PLANETARE seeks a postdoctoral researcher with a background in stellar magnetism and/or exoplanetary science to develop novel ways of detecting and characterizing the mutual influence of stars and planets with a focus on the influence of planets in short orbits on the magnetism of their host stars. At the core of the project is a new way to find exoplanets: detecting them through their magnetic interaction with the host star. This position builds the observational foundation - the sample, the activity catalog, and the geometry of the systems - and confirms any transiting planets among the interacting systems.Your Tasks- Compile the most accurate and complete flaring activity catalog to date using space-borne photometry- Search the sample of flaring stars for transiting planet candidates using space-borne photometry- Constrain the orientation of the rotational and magnetic axes of interacting systems- Measure stellar activity characteristics and their predictive power for interactionThe transit search, flaring catalog and geometry measurements will constrain some of the drivers of interaction and its observability, working towards a true occurrence rate of magnetic interaction in young star-planet systems. You will work closely with a second postdoc (https://karriere.mps.mpg.de/jobposting/ff58b9b82b6efc0b224bf8134f1471929fdc639c0) within a small, newly formed team of two postdocs and a PhD student, led by the PI (Ekaterina Ilin). jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to detect exoplanets through magnetic star-planet interaction (Astrophysiker/in, Astronom/in)
jobs.description: The Max Planck Institute for Solar System Research (MPS) in Göttingen is one of the world's leading research institutions in the field of solar physics and planetary research with around 300 employees. The interdisciplinary research focus is the investigation of the development, diversity and dynamics of planets, moons, small bodies, the sun and solar-like stars. The MPS develops and operates scientific instruments for current and future space missions (e.g. ESA, NASA), and carries out cosmochemical laboratory investigations of meteorites as well as numerical modeling on state-of-the-art supercomputers.The Department Solar & Stellar Interiors at MPS invites applications for the position of aPostdoctoral Researcher (f/m/d) to detect exoplanets through magnetic star-planet interactionIn recent years, exoplanetary science has undergone a major shift -- moving from exoplanet detection towards understanding star-planet systems as a whole, including the host star, interplanetary medium and galactic context. Specifically, tidal and magnetic interactions between planets and their host stars have been recognized to be able to modulate the evolution of both, including the atmospheric evolution of the planet and its habitability. The newly established ERC StG project PLANETARE seeks a postdoctoral researcher with a background in stellar magnetism and/or exoplanetary science to develop novel ways of detecting and characterizing the mutual influence of stars and planets with a focus on the influence of planets in short orbits on the magnetism of their host stars. At the core of the project is a new way to find exoplanets: detecting them through their magnetic interaction with the host star. This position develops the detection method itself, i.e., the statistics, the search, and the physical model behind it.Your Tasks- Develop new statistical techniques to identify signatures of planet-induced flaring- Identify young stars and search them for planet-induced flaring using archival and upcoming Kepler, TESS, and PLATO observations- Measure how the strength and frequency of planet-induced flaring change as systems age- Develop a forward model of the magnetic feedback loop between planet and starThe derived occurrence rates of planet-induced flaring constrain the prevalence of interaction; the modeling of the evolution and mechanism will be built on the largest survey for planet-induced flaring to date.
